items.change: The party arrived in Brandonsford following a treasure map whose marked locations they did not recognize.
items.impact_basis: Beat_1 establishes the party's reason for being in this unknown land, setting up their overarching pursuit.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_1's unresolved map will drive later Sessions as the party seeks the treasure.

items.change: Reginald the frog warned Dr. Uriah that a trickster Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into town every night.
items.impact_basis: Beat_6 reveals a new nightly danger in town that the party should avoid.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_6's nightly creature likely ties into other town troubles and will probably come up again.

items.change: Eric the Reeve offered 1000 gold for the body of a black dragon troubling Brandonsford, and the party gathered accounts of it.
items.impact_basis: Beats 15, 16 and 27 give the party a major bounty and details of a black dragon, a likely main goal.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_15's open bounty on a living dragon will shape later Sessions.

items.change: Lady Hilda offered to join the party's dragon hunt for pay, and Sir Phidipaldi promised to return for her services.
items.impact_basis: Beat_10 introduces a seasoned potential hireling for the dragon hunt.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_10's pending promise to return makes her likely to reappear.

items.change: Drop Dead Ned offered himself and his killer wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, and Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.
items.impact_basis: Beats 21 and 22 present a dangerous, murderous hireling option.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_22's open offer may come up again if the party seeks help.

items.change: The party learned that shipments to Brandonsford have stopped arriving for months, leaving the town short of goods.
items.impact_basis: Beats 13 and 30 reveal a town-wide supply problem with an unknown cause.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_13 and beat_30 describe an unexplained mystery likely to be investigated later.

items.change: Sir Phidipaldi insulted Eric the Reeve and challenged him to a duel, and Bentley sent him off to the Golden Egg for the night.
items.impact_basis: Beats 17, 19 and 23 sour relations with the town's quest-giver and get Sir Phidipaldi ejected from the inn.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_19's unresolved ill will with the Reeve who offers the bounty is likely to matter again.

items.change: Farmer Gill offered Dunk the mule Shamus for 100 gold or the dragon's death, and Dunk slept in Gill's barn to think it over.
items.impact_basis: Beats 25 and 29 present a minor purchase offer and a night's lodging.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_25's offer for an ordinary mule is a small matter that may briefly resurface.

items.change: Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help Quinn stage a fake ale shipment to get back at Bentley, for 100 gold.
items.impact_basis: Beats 35 and 36 give Sir Phidipaldi a paid scheme and reveal Quinn's nightly vanishing stock.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_36's agreed but unperformed scheme will likely be carried out in a later Session.

items.change: Dunk learned that Warwick the smith displays a superb mithril chain shirt that he refuses to sell.
items.impact_basis: Beat_31 notes a valuable item in town but changes nothing yet.
items.lasting_basis: Beat_31's mithril shirt may draw interest later but is not pursued.

items.change: The night watchman let the party into Brandonsford after Sir Phidipaldi invoked Zeus's law of hospitality.
items.impact_basis: Beats 3 and 4 cover a routine entry into town and orientation.
items.lasting_basis: The entry in beat_3 matters mostly within the Session.
items.encounter_basis: The arrival is mostly logistics; the meaningful part, the treasure map, is already told by thread_1.

items.change: Dr. Uriah spoke with Reginald the frog, who warned of the Clurichen.
items.impact_basis: Beat_6 delivers the Clurichen warning; beat_5 is colour.
items.lasting_basis: The warning in beat_6 is likely to matter again.
items.encounter_basis: The frog conversation's only substance is the Clurichen warning, which thread_2 already tells.

items.change: At the Clumsy Fox the party learned of the dragon bounty, met potential hirelings, and Sir Phidipaldi's quarrel with the Reeve got him sent away.
items.impact_basis: Beats 10, 15, 19, 22 and 23 introduce the bounty, hirelings and a feud.
items.lasting_basis: The bounty in beat_15 and the feud in beat_19 will shape later Sessions.
items.encounter_basis: The tavern night is pivotal, but its central events (bounty, Hilda, Ned, Reeve quarrel) are each told by their own threads.

items.change: Dunk spent the evening with Farmer Gill, who offered his mule, shared Brandonsford's dragon history and town gossip, and hosted him in his barn.
items.impact_basis: Beats 26, 27 and 29 provide lore and hospitality, adding modestly to the dragon situation.
items.lasting_basis: Gill's hospitality and lore in beats 26 and 29 may matter again, as his sons are hunting the dragon.
items.encounter_basis: Dunk's solitary night of hospitality and lore with Gill gives personal context distinct from the mule purchase and the dragon bounty.

items.change: At the Golden Egg, Sir Phidipaldi heard Quinn's complaint of vanishing stock and agreed to stage a fake shipment against Bentley.
items.impact_basis: Beats 35 and 36 create a paid scheme.
items.lasting_basis: The scheme in beat_36 is pending.
items.encounter_basis: The central interaction is the agreement with Quinn, already told by thread_9.
